seoTitle: Brute-Force and Scan Detector for Access Logs
metaDescription: List IPs with failed login bursts, many 404s or requests for known probe paths in an access log. Findings are for review. Free.
intro: Finds failed login bursts, 404 bursts and probe path requests per IP.
why:
Public servers are probed all day. The useful question is which IPs look automated and what they asked for. This tool applies three simple rules.

A burst of 401 or 403 on a login-like path, a burst of 404 responses, and a short list of well-known probe patterns such as wp-login.php or .env. A match is worth a look, not proof of an attack. Shared NAT addresses and monitoring tools can trigger the rules.
howTo: Read the IP list and the reasons.
Block or rate-limit only after checking.

faq.q: Why is a probe on a 404 still listed?
faq.a: The request itself is the signal. A 404 means the server had nothing there.
